usedTryThisNowFrames: the-12-week-year-ch01: Write one result you keep calling important, then name the weekly pattern that keeps proving it is not protected yet.
the-12-week-year-ch02: Take one annual goal and rewrite the next proof of progress as something that must be visible within 12 weeks.
the-12-week-year-ch03: For one avoided action, write the future person who benefits and the specific discomfort you are asking yourself to tolerate.
the-12-week-year-ch04: Circle one goal in your current plan and cross out every listed action that would not matter inside the next 12 weeks.
the-12-week-year-ch05: Pick one 12 week goal and write the one weekly action that must happen before Friday for it to stay alive.
the-12-week-year-ch06: Write the one number or yes-no proof that would tell you whether this week moved your goal or only felt busy.
the-12-week-year-ch07: Block one 45-minute execution slot this week and write the specific request you will refuse to keep it intact.
the-12-week-year-ch08: Name one condition you have been blaming, then write the next action you still own even if that condition stays unchanged.
the-12-week-year-ch09: Write one goal in two columns: what interest says you will do, and what commitment requires when the week gets inconvenient.
the-12-week-year-ch10: Before your next important action, say what greatness would look like in that exact 10-minute window.
the-12-week-year-ch11: Name one thing that deserves extra weight this week and one thing you will deliberately under-serve without pretending otherwise.
the-12-week-year-ch12: Draw a three-step loop for one goal: action taken, score seen, adjustment made before the next week starts.
the-12-week-year-ch13: Write one sentence that describes the life or team result your current 12 week effort is meant to serve.
the-12-week-year-ch14: For one 12 week goal, write the goal, the lead action, and the weekly proof that the action happened.
the-12-week-year-ch15: Schedule a 20-minute weekly review for this week and invite one person who should know what you are committing to execute.
the-12-week-year-ch16: Choose one lead action and mark a simple weekly score: planned count, completed count, and what must change next week.
the-12-week-year-ch17: Place one Performance Time block on tomorrow's calendar and move one reactive task outside it before the day begins.
the-12-week-year-ch18: For one missed action, write the constraint, then write the one ownership action you can take without waiting for the constraint to vanish.
the-12-week-year-ch19: Tell one specific person the action you will complete this week, when it will be done, and how they can verify it.
the-12-week-year-ch20: Label your current cycle pressure as immediate gratification, old habit, victim thinking, or too many goals, then choose the next correction.
the-12-week-year-ch21: Write three bullets for the cycle that just ended: keep, change, and recommit before the next 12 weeks begin.
